title: Ethiopian 8-Contact Antenatal Care (ANC) Model
sourceOrganization: Ethiopian Federal Ministry of Health (FMoH) & WHO
summary: Ethiopia adopted the WHO 8-contact antenatal model to ensure timely screening, fetal growth monitoring, and maternal complication prevention.
keyPoints: Contact 1: Before 12 weeks of pregnancy (gestational dating, baseline lab tests, IFA initiation).
Contact 2: At 20 weeks (fetal anatomy ultrasound check, blood pressure check).
Contact 3: At 26 weeks; Contact 4: At 30 weeks; Contact 5: At 34 weeks.
Contacts 6, 7 & 8: At 36, 38, and 40 weeks (delivery planning, presentation check, danger sign vigilance).
detailedContent: The 8-contact ANC model replaces the outdated 4-visit schedule, providing maternal health teams continuous touchpoints to detect hypertensive disorders, gestational diabetes, severe anemia, and fetal distress.
In Ethiopia, Health Extension Workers register pregnant women at the household level and link them to Woreda Health Centers for clinical examinations and ultrasound services.
whenToSeeClinician: Book your first ANC checkup before 12 weeks of pregnancy at your local Kebele Health Post or Health Center.
ethiopiaContext: Provided free of charge in all Ethiopian public primary healthcare units under the national maternal health mandate.

title: Critical Pregnancy Danger Signs & Emergency Triage
summary: Key obstetric warning signs requiring immediate emergency medical care: vaginal bleeding, severe headache with visual blur, and reduced fetal movement.
keyPoints: Vaginal bleeding at any stage of pregnancy is an acute medical emergency.
Severe persistent headache, blurred vision, or sudden facial edema indicates pre-eclampsia.
Reduced or absent baby kicks (fewer than 10 kicks in 2 hours during third trimester) warrants immediate hospital assessment.
High fever, shivering, or foul-smelling amniotic fluid signals serious intrauterine infection.
detailedContent: Obstetric danger signs cannot wait for scheduled clinic appointments. Waiting at home for symptoms to subside poses life-threatening hazards to mother and fetus.
Emergency transport can be mobilized in Ethiopia by calling 907 (Red Cross Ambulance) or 8335 (FMoH National Helpline).
whenToSeeClinician: Go immediately to the nearest hospital maternity ward or emergency department. Do not wait.
ethiopiaContext: Ambulance dispatch available via 907 (Red Cross) or 952 (Addis Ababa EMS) and free emergency triage at public hospitals.

title: Daily Iron and Folic Acid (IFA) Supplementation
summary: Daily oral iron (60mg elemental iron) and folic acid (400mcg) throughout pregnancy prevents maternal anemia, puerperal sepsis, and low birth weight.
keyPoints: Take 1 tablet daily starting as early as possible in pregnancy.
Folic acid prevents neural tube defects (spina bifida); iron prevents severe maternal anemia and exhaustion.
Common side effects: dark-colored stool, mild nausea; take with food or before bedtime with water.
Avoid taking iron with tea, coffee, or milk which inhibit iron absorption; citrus juice (vitamin C) enhances absorption.
detailedContent: Maternal anemia remains a major contributor to postpartum hemorrhage morbidity in Ethiopia.
The Ethiopian Federal Ministry of Health distributes free 90-day IFA blister packs to all pregnant women at ANC visits.
whenToSeeClinician: Obtain your free IFA supply at your local Kebele Health Post or discuss non-constipating formulations if nausea occurs.
ethiopiaContext: Supplied free at public health centers and community health posts throughout Ethiopia.

title: Gestational Diabetes & Hypertensive Screening Protocols
summary: Draft summary on oral glucose tolerance tests (OGTT) at 24 to 28 weeks and automated blood pressure monitoring during routine ANC visits.
keyPoints: Gestational diabetes develops during pregnancy and increases risks of macrosomia (large baby) and birth trauma.
Screening with a 75g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) between 24 and 28 gestational weeks.
Gestational hypertension requires regular urine protein testing to differentiate from pre-eclampsia.
Dietary management and monitored physical activity form the first line of therapy.
detailedContent: Draft clinical notes: Protocol standardization between tertiary referral hospitals and regional health centers is currently undergoing ESOG review.
Not yet ratified as unified national protocol across all tier-1 health centers.
whenToSeeClinician: Ask your midwife or doctor about blood sugar and urine protein checks during your 24 to 28 week ANC check.
ethiopiaContext: Under review by the Ethiopian Society of Obstetricians & Gynecologists.

title: Positive Home Pregnancy Test: Confirmation, ANC Initiation, and Care Options
sourceOrganization: World Health Organization (WHO) & Ethiopian Federal Ministry of Health (FMoH)
summary: A positive home urine pregnancy test detects human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG). Next steps include clinical confirmation to rule out ectopic pregnancy, initiating early antenatal care (ANC), and exploring compassionate options.
keyPoints: Clinical Confirmation: Home urine tests detect hCG with high accuracy, but cannot rule out ectopic pregnancy (pregnancy outside the uterus). An in-person clinical exam or early ultrasound is recommended.
Early Prenatal Care: If you wish to continue the pregnancy, start daily Iron and Folic Acid (IFA) immediately and schedule Contact 1 of Ethiopia's 8-contact ANC model before 12 weeks.

Options Counseling: If the pregnancy is unintended or you are unsure, safe, confidential, non-judgmental options counseling is legally accessible in Ethiopia through Marie Stopes (helpline 8044), FGAE, and public health centers.
Healthy Habits: Avoid alcohol, tobacco, and unprescribed medications; stay hydrated and eat iron-rich foods.
detailedContent: Finding out you are pregnant can bring mixed feelings. In Ethiopia, primary healthcare units provide confidential care whether you are continuing the pregnancy or seeking options counseling.
Early clinical confirmation checks maternal blood pressure, hemoglobin, and screens for asymptomatic conditions like bacteriuria and syphilis.
whenToSeeClinician: Visit your local Kebele Health Post or Woreda Health Center within 1-2 weeks for ultrasound confirmation and ANC registration, or call Marie Stopes toll-free at 8044 for confidential options counseling.
ethiopiaContext: Free ANC and IFA at all Ethiopian public health centers; confidential options counseling via Marie Stopes helpline 8044.
